learning.learning_goal: Understand shared-equally division as finding the size of each equal group.
learning.big_idea: Division can answer how much each group receives when one total is shared equally.
novice_success_criteria: name the total and number of groups
explain why groups must be equal
find and verify one group's share

screens.label: Lesson 005 · Prototype
screens.title: What does each group receive?
screens.body: Start with one total, choose how many equal groups will receive it, and find the amount in one group.
screens.callout: No division vocabulary is assumed. We will build the idea from sharing.

screens.label: Misconception
screens.title: Do groups always mean multiply?
screens.prompt: Twelve markers are shared equally among 3 tables. What does each table receive?

choices.text: 4 markers, because three equal groups of 4 rebuild 12
choices.feedback: The total is 12 and there are 3 receiving groups. Sharing one marker to each table repeatedly gives 4 per table; 3 × 4 rebuilds 12.

hints: Keep the total at 12; do not create more markers.
Deal the markers one at a time to 3 tables until none remain.

visual.ariaLabel: Twelve counters arranged as three equal groups with four counters in each group
visual.message: The same total is reorganized into 3 equal groups.

screens.label: Discover
screens.title: What quantity did the sharing find?

visual.ariaLabel: Three equal groups containing four counters each
visual.message: Every group receives 4; nothing is added or removed.

choices.feedback: Shared-equally division finds one group's size when the total and number of groups are known.

hints: The problem already told us there are 3 groups.
Look inside one group and count its markers.

screens.label: Language
screens.title: Name every part of the relationship.

visual.ariaLabel: Three equal groups of four counters
visual.message: 12 is the total, 3 is the number of groups, and 4 is one equal share.

screens.guidance: Ask what is known before choosing an operation: total, number of groups, or size of each group?

screens.label: Remember
screens.title: Total shared into groups gives one share.
screens.hook: Total ÷ number of groups = amount in each group
screens.body: Rebuild the division from the story instead of reacting to a keyword.
rebuildSteps: Name how many equal groups receive it.
Distribute until every group has the same amount.
Multiply groups by one share to check the total.
screens.boundary: This model finds group size. A different division question may give the group size and ask how many groups can be made.

screens.label: Symbol
screens.title: Which equation describes the equal sharing?

visual.ariaLabel: Twelve counters in three equal groups of four
visual.message: The equation must keep 12 as the total and find one share.

choices.feedback: Twelve shared among 3 equal groups gives 4 in each group.

hints: The answer describes what one of the 3 groups receives.

screens.label: Reveal
screens.title: Division and multiplication describe the same groups.

visual.ariaLabel: Three equal groups of four counters
visual.message: Three groups of 4 recombine into the original total of 12.

screens.label: Guided practice
screens.title: Share 15 bottles among 5 shelves.

visual.ariaLabel: Fifteen counters arranged in five equal groups of three
visual.message: Count one shelf only after confirming all 5 shelves are equal.

choices.feedback: Five equal shelves with 3 bottles each rebuild the total: 5 × 3 = 15.

hints: Use all 15 bottles without changing the total.
Deal one bottle to each of 5 shelves, then repeat.

screens.label: Independent practice
screens.title: Solve without the model.
screens.prompt: Twenty-four feet of board is cut into 8 equal sections. How long is each section?

choices.feedback: 24 ÷ 8 = 3, and eight sections of 3 feet rebuild 24 feet.

hints: Name the total length and the number of equal sections.
Find a length that can be repeated 8 times to rebuild 24.

screens.label: Recall
screens.title: Reconstruct the idea.
screens.prompt: When a total is shared equally and the number of groups is known, what does division find?

choices.feedback: Division finds one equal share in this kind of problem.

choices.text: Whether the groups may be unequal

hints: The total and group count are already known.
Ask what remains unknown inside each group.

screens.label: Transfer
screens.title: Use equal sharing in a new setting.
screens.prompt: A cyclist travels 42 miles over 6 days, the same distance each day. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: The cyclist travels 36 miles each day because 42 − 6 = 36
The cyclist travels 252 miles each day because 42 × 6 = 252
The cyclist travels 7 miles each day because 6 × 7 = 42
choices.feedback: The 42-mile total is shared across 6 equal days, and 6 daily shares of 7 miles rebuild 42.

hints: Keep the total distance at 42 miles.
Find the daily distance that repeated 6 times equals 42.

screens.label: Reflect
screens.title: Which explanation shows understanding?
screens.prompt: Choose the statement that explains shared-equally division.

choices.text: Groups always tell me to multiply.
I keep the total fixed, make equal groups, and find one group's share.
Division answers every grouping question in exactly the same way.

hints: The operation comes from what is unknown.
Think about how the multiplication check used the original total.

screens.title: You rebuilt an equal share.
screens.body: You connected a fixed total, equal groups, division, and a multiplication check.
screens.nextRecommendation: Prototype next: numerator and denominator meaning.
